The volt (symbol: V), named after Alessandro Volta, is the unit of measurement of electric potential, electric potential difference (voltage), and electromotive force in the International System of Units (SI).
One volt is defined as the electric potential between two points of a conducting wire when an electric current of one ampere dissipates one watt of power between those points.

It can be expressed in terms of SI base units (m, kg, s, and A) as V=powerelectric current=WA=kg⋅m2⋅s−3A=kg⋅m2⋅s−3⋅A−1.
Equivalently, it is the potential difference between two points that will impart one joule of energy per coulomb of charge that passes through it. It can be expressed in terms of SI base units (m, kg, s, and A) as V=potential energycharge=JC=kg⋅m2⋅s−2A⋅s=kg⋅m2⋅s−3⋅A−1.
